fee_detail: Alabama issues no marriage license. Mobile County Probate Court charges $73 to record the Alabama Marriage Certificate form; each county probate court sets its own recording fee.
validity_detail: No license is issued. The notarized Alabama Marriage Certificate form must be delivered to a probate court within 30 days of the later spouse signature.

fee_detail: $60 application fee, set by the state. The application form lists $73 for licenses mailed out.
waiting_period_detail: Three business days after a completed application is received by the issuing office.
validity_detail: The application is valid for one year, but once the license is issued and picked up it is valid for 90 days.

fee_detail: $98. The Clerk of Court takes cash, money order, or credit card; justice courts that issue licenses take money orders only.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period is stated; the page says the license may be used the same day it is received.
validity_detail: Valid for one year from the date of issue.

fee_detail: $60, paid by cash or credit card (no checks) at the Pulaski County Circuit/County Clerk. Card payments carry an added processing fee.
waiting_period_detail: None when all applicants are 18 or older. Applications involving anyone under 18 have a five-business-day wait.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days from the date of issue, according to the Clark County Clerk.

fee_detail: Los Angeles County lists $91 for a public marriage license and $85 for a confidential license. A county notice says higher fees ($176 and $220) take effect 30 days after a fee ordinance is adopted.
waiting_period_detail: None. The Siskiyou County Clerk states there is no waiting period between receiving a marriage license and the ceremony.
validity_detail: The license is valid for 90 days.

fee_detail: $30.00 at the El Paso County Clerk and Recorder, cash or debit/credit card only.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period is stated; the license is valid when issued.
validity_detail: Valid upon issue and must be used in Colorado within 35 days.

fee_detail: $50 per license, paid to the town where the marriage will take place.
waiting_period_detail: At least 48 hours after the second spouse signs the application before the town can issue the license; the page says this is in effect starting October 1, 2026.
validity_detail: The license is good for up to 65 days after the town gives it to you; the wedding must be within that time.

fee_detail: $70 if either applicant is a Delaware resident; $120 if neither is. The schedule also lists a $5 processing fee and a $20 background form fee.
waiting_period_detail: 24-hour wait after the license is issued before the ceremony. The county FAQ says it can be waived if either party is active-duty military or critically ill.
validity_detail: Valid for 30 days after issuance. Extensions of 30, 60 or 90 days are available for an extra fee.

fee_detail: $45 application fee. $35 of it is waived if an original DC Domestic Partnership Certificate is presented. Payment by cash, card, or check or money order.
waiting_period_detail: DC Courts says you can get married any time after you receive your license, including the same day you receive it.
validity_detail: A marriage license does not expire once issued.

fee_detail: $86 for a marriage license at the Miami-Dade Clerk. Other Florida counties may charge a different total.
waiting_period_detail: 3 days for Florida residents. Waived if the couple completes a premarital course and presents the certificate. Non-Florida residents have no waiting period.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days after issuance.

fee_detail: $68.50, which includes one mailed certified copy of the marriage certificate.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period after the license is issued before the ceremony can take place, per the Franklin County Probate Court.
validity_detail: The license does not have an expiration date.

fee_detail: $65 total: a $60 application fee plus a $5 portal fee. Fees are non-refundable.
waiting_period_detail: None. The ceremony can take place right after the license is issued.
validity_detail: The ceremony must be held within 30 days of picking up the license, or the license is void.

fee_detail: $30 at the Ada County Recorder, payable by card (with a service fee), cash, or check.
waiting_period_detail: None. You may marry the same day the license is issued.
validity_detail: The Ada County page says the license has no expiration date.

fee_detail: $60 at the Cook County Clerk. Fee is waived for couples converting a civil union to a marriage within 60 days of applying.
waiting_period_detail: The license becomes effective 1 day after it is issued, so there is a one-day wait before the ceremony.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days from the date of issuance. A ceremony after expiration is not valid.

fee_detail: $25 if one or both applicants are Indiana residents; $65 for out-of-state residents. Some offices add a $4 document fee.
waiting_period_detail: None. A license is valid from issuance, and couples may marry as early as the same day.
validity_detail: 60 days from the date it is issued. After that the couple must apply for a new license.

fee_detail: $35, due at application, nonrefundable, and includes one certified copy of the marriage certificate. A waiver of the waiting period adds $5.
waiting_period_detail: License becomes valid after three calendar days from the date of application (application day not counted). A district judge can waive this for an extra $5.
validity_detail: The license does not expire once it has been picked up, per the Polk County Recorder. If it is not retrieved from the county registrar within six months of the application date, the application becomes void.

fee_detail: $85.50 for the license in Johnson County, the largest county. Card payment adds $2.14 and e-check adds $1.25. Fees are nonrefundable.
waiting_period_detail: No license before the third calendar day after the application is filed, counting Sundays and holidays. A district judge can waive the wait in emergencies or extraordinary circumstances.
validity_detail: Six months from the date of issuance. The license expires if the marriage does not take place within that time.

fee_detail: $60 in Boone County, collected by the county clerk when the license is issued. The fee is nonrefundable.
waiting_period_detail: None. The Franklin County Clerk states there is no waiting period, blood test, or physical requirement for a Kentucky marriage license.
validity_detail: 30 days, counting the date of issue. After that the license is invalid.

fee_detail: $27.50 for a license from the Orleans Parish Marriage Office, run by the Louisiana Department of Health. Cash, check, money order and credit or debit cards are accepted; fees are nonrefundable.
waiting_period_detail: 24 hours must pass between issuance of the license and the ceremony, unless a Justice of the Peace grants a waiver.
validity_detail: Valid for 30 days from the date of issuance.

fee_detail: $40 to obtain a marriage license (filed as notice of intentions with a municipal clerk or Maine Vital Records).
waiting_period_detail: None. Once intentions are filed, the license may be issued immediately.
validity_detail: The license is void if not used within 90 days from the day the intentions were filed.

fee_detail: $55 for the application and license in Montgomery County, paid by cash or Visa or Mastercard. Personal checks are not accepted.
waiting_period_detail: The license must be purchased at least 48 hours before the ceremony. State law makes it effective at 6 a.m. on the second calendar day after issuance.
validity_detail: Valid for six months.

fee_detail: $50 at Cambridge City Hall (Middlesex County). Boston's Registry also lists $50.
waiting_period_detail: 3 days between filing the marriage intention and using the license; a court order can waive the wait.
validity_detail: 60 days from the date of application.

fee_detail: $30 if one or both applicants live in Wayne County; $40 if both live outside Michigan.
waiting_period_detail: 3 days including the application date. The clerk may issue sooner for good cause, for a fee set by the county board.
validity_detail: The license is void unless the marriage is solemnized within 33 days after the application.

fee_detail: $125 for the license, set in state law.
waiting_period_detail: None. A 2016 law eliminated the waiting period, and Anoka County says the marriage may occur the same day.
validity_detail: Six months.

fee_detail: $37 in DeSoto County, payable by cash or card; the clerk charges a processing fee on credit card payments.
waiting_period_detail: None. The DeSoto County Circuit Clerk says no blood work or waiting period is required.
validity_detail: The license does not expire once it has been issued, according to the DeSoto County Circuit Clerk.

fee_detail: $53 at the Clay County Recorder of Deeds, payable by cash or credit card; the card processor adds a transaction fee.
waiting_period_detail: None. The Cape Girardeau County Recorder says there is no waiting period and the license can be used the day it is issued.
validity_detail: The license is void 30 days after it is issued.

fee_detail: $53, set in state law.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period. The license is valid the minute it is issued, per the Beaverhead County Clerk of District Court.
validity_detail: Effective when issued; expires after 180 days.

fee_detail: $50 for the license, set in state law, effective July 18, 2026.
waiting_period_detail: None. Dodge County says licenses are issued the same day when requirements are met.
validity_detail: The license must be used within one year of issuance.

fee_detail: $102 at the Clark County Clerk. Card payments carry an extra fee and checks are not accepted.
waiting_period_detail: None. You can marry as soon as you have the license.
validity_detail: The license expires one year from the date it is issued.

fee_detail: $50, set by state law and paid by the couple to the town or city clerk.
waiting_period_detail: None. There is no waiting period in New Hampshire.
validity_detail: The license is valid for up to 90 days from the date of filing.

fee_detail: $28 application fee, paid to the local registrar. A new application and another $28 are needed if the license expires unused.
waiting_period_detail: 72 hours after the application is filed with the local registrar, before the license is issued. No waiting period for a remarriage of an existing marriage.
validity_detail: Once issued, the license is good for 30 days. The application itself is valid for six months from the date filed.

fee_detail: $55 at the county clerk, a statewide fee raised from $25 by Senate Bill 290 in June 2025. Cash or card (no American Express).
waiting_period_detail: None. The license is ready immediately.
validity_detail: The Bernalillo County Clerk says licenses do not expire.

fee_detail: $35 at the New York City Clerk (Brooklyn is the largest borough). Outside NYC, town and city clerks charge $40.
waiting_period_detail: 24 hours after the license is issued before the ceremony. A judge can waive it; the waiver is free from the borough County Clerk.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 calendar days starting the day after issue. Active-duty military may get 180 days with proof at application.

fee_detail: $60 for issuing a license, set in state law and charged by every county register of deeds.
waiting_period_detail: No required waiting period between the issuance of the marriage license and the wedding. The license must be issued before the wedding.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days from the date of issuance, and it must be returned to the issuing office.

fee_detail: $65 at the Cass County Finance Office (Fargo). Cash, check or card; cards add a fee. Other counties may charge less.
waiting_period_detail: None. You can marry right after the license is issued.
validity_detail: The license must be used within 60 days. Unused licenses expire with no refund.

fee_detail: $65 at the Franklin County Probate Court. Ohio fees vary by county.
waiting_period_detail: None for adults once the application is accepted.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days from the date it is issued.

fee_detail: $50 license fee at the Oklahoma County Court Clerk.
waiting_period_detail: None for applicants 18 or older. Applicants under 18 face a 72 hour wait.
validity_detail: Valid for 30 days from the date issued; the ceremony and return must happen within that time.

fee_detail: $60, plus $5 more to waive the three-day waiting period.
waiting_period_detail: Wait 3 days after the license is issued before the ceremony; the wait can be waived for an extra $5.
validity_detail: Effective 3 days after issue, then valid for 60 days.

fee_detail: $90 for a regular license; $100 for a Quaker or self-uniting license.
waiting_period_detail: A license cannot be issued before the third day after applying; a court may allow it sooner in emergencies or for called-up reservists.
validity_detail: Valid starting the third day after application and for 60 days from the issue date.

fee_detail: $24, paid to the city or town clerk issuing the license.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period. The Cranston City Clerk says the license is issued when you come in.
validity_detail: The license is good for 90 days.

fee_detail: $50 for Greenville County residents, $75 for other South Carolina residents, $115 for out-of-state residents.
waiting_period_detail: 24 hours between filing the application and issuance of the license.
validity_detail: South Carolina marriage licenses do not expire.

fee_detail: $40. Some Registers of Deeds may take only cash or traveler's checks.
waiting_period_detail: No waiting period and no blood test.
validity_detail: The marriage must take place within 90 days of buying the license or it becomes void.

fee_detail: $99.50 in cash or $101.49 by card at the Davidson County Clerk in Nashville. A notarized premarital counseling certificate saves $60.
waiting_period_detail: None. The Montgomery County Clerk says there is not a waiting period and the license is issued the same day you apply.
validity_detail: Valid for 30 days from issuance, counted under state rules.

fee_detail: $81 for the standard license; $181 if no applicant shows Texas residency on a valid ID.
waiting_period_detail: 72 hours after purchase. Waived with a premarital course certificate, and automatically for active military with military ID.
validity_detail: The officiant should sign the license within 90 days of the date it was issued.

fee_detail: $50 (card, cash or check).
waiting_period_detail: None. You can marry as soon as you have the license.
validity_detail: The license is valid for 32 days, then it expires if the marriage has not been solemnized.

fee_detail: $80 at any Vermont town or city clerk.
waiting_period_detail: None.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 days from the date issued; the license is void if no authorized person performs the ceremony in that time.

fee_detail: $30 (cash or card; cards carry a 4% fee).
waiting_period_detail: None once the license is issued; no blood test.
validity_detail: Valid for 60 calendar days. The marriage must take place in Virginia.

fee_detail: $169 application fee (cash, check, money order or card).
waiting_period_detail: Three days before the license can be used. King County counts from issuance and says it cannot be waived, even by court order.
validity_detail: The license is void if the marriage is not solemnized within 60 days of issuance.

fee_detail: $55 under state law.
waiting_period_detail: None stated. Fayette County says licenses are effective immediately after issue.
validity_detail: The license is void if the marriage is not solemnized within 60 days of issuance.

fee_detail: $120 in Milwaukee County, paid when the application is filed and nonrefundable. Cash and credit or debit cards are accepted (3% card convenience fee); no personal checks.
waiting_period_detail: 3 days after application; the county clerk may issue sooner for an extra fee of up to $25.
validity_detail: Authorizes the ceremony within 60 days of issuance.

fee_detail: $30.00, which includes the first official certificate. A reprint of a certificate is $5.00.
waiting_period_detail: None. There is no waiting period or residency requirement.
validity_detail: Expires one year from the date of issuance if the marriage has not been solemnized.
